result.note: Tests the Principal Purpose Test in the India–Mauritius DTAA, the 2017 grandfathering cut-off, BEPS alignment and the court behind the Tiger Global ruling. The retroactive versus prospective point is avoided because the story is internally inconsistent on it.

questions.prompt: In October 2026, the CBDT notified changes to India's Double Taxation Avoidance Agreement with Mauritius. Consider the following statements:
items: The changes allow tax authorities to deny treaty benefits if obtaining them was one of the principal purposes of an arrangement.
Capital gains on shares acquired before April 1, 2017 lose their earlier grandfathering protection.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explain: Statement 2 is wrong because capital gains on shares acquired before April 1, 2017 remain protected under the earlier grandfathering rules. Dividends, interest and post-2017 capital gains are the items that face sharper scrutiny under the Principal Purpose Test.
questions.source: Capital gains on shares acquired before April 1, 2017 remain protected under previous grandfathering rules.

questions.prompt: Consider the following statements about the Principal Purpose Test introduced into the India–Mauritius tax treaty in October 2026:
items: It was notified by the Central Board of Direct Taxes.
It aligns India with global Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) anti-abuse standards.
Mauritius holding companies must show real substance, local governance and a clear non-tax commercial objective to avoid tax demands.
questions.ask: Which of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explain: All three statements match the story. The CBDT notified the change, it brings India in line with BEPS anti-abuse standards, and holding companies can no longer rely on paper presence. TBB expects risk-averse funds to shift towards higher-substance jurisdictions such as Singapore or the UAE.
questions.source: It aligns India with global Base Erosion and Profit Shifting (BEPS) anti-abuse standards.

questions.prompt: Which body delivered the January 2026 Tiger Global ruling, which held that grandfathering does not automatically shield shell structures lacking commercial substance from domestic anti-avoidance rules?
questions.explain: The Supreme Court's January 2026 Tiger Global ruling set this precedent. The ruling sharpens the risk for Mauritius conduits even where shares fall within the pre-2017 grandfathering window.
questions.source: the Supreme Court's January 2026 Tiger Global ruling set a precedent that grandfathering doesn't automatically shield shell structures that lack real commercial substance from domestic anti-avoidance rules.
